To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the short form version (RADS SF; Reynolds, 2002) of the Reynolds Adolescent Depresssion Scale (RADS; Reynolds, 1999) is a reliable and valid self-report measure of depression that is equivalent across gender, age groups, and ethnic groups in a large population sample of New Zealand adolescents.
the RADS SF is an equivalent measure of depression in New Zealand secondary school adolescents across gender, ethnic groups, age, and socioeconomic status.
the RADS SF has good reliability and validity and is equivalent across age, gender, and ethnic groups in a large population-based sample of New Zealand adolescents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the equivalence of a short form of the RADS for measuring depression in a large sample of secondary school students in New Zealand.
the equivalence of the Short Form version of the Reynolds Adolescence Depression Scale (RASD-SF) across gender, age and ethnic groups in a New Zealand adolescent population.
the development of a new instrument to measure depression in adolescents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the RADS SF is equivalent across gender, age (within the 12-18 age range), and ethnicity (New Zealand European; Maori; Pacific; Asian; Other), for measuring depression in a population of New Zealand secondary school aged adolescents.
the RADS SF is a valid and reliable measure of depression in adolescents across the age range of 11 to 17 years and across ethnic groups and gender.
the RADS-SF is equivalent for measuring depression across age groups, ethnic groups, gender groups and in a New Zealand population.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RADS SF can be reliably used with New Zealand adolescents across the age range 11 to 18 years and across ethnic groups.
the RADS SF is a reliable and valid measure of depression in a New Zealand adolescent population and can be used with confidence for research and clinical practice.
the RADS SF is a reliable and valid tool for measuring adolescent depression across a range of demographic variables in New Zealand adolescents.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RADS SF is a valid and reliable instrument for measuring depression in a large and diverse adolescent population.
the short version of RADS is a reliable and valid tool for measuring depression in New Zealand adolescents.
the RADS SF can be used with confidence in New Zealand adolescents across gender, ethnic, and age groups. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2018 APA, all rights reserved)
